description: One row per customer meeting or call that was processed from a transcript or notes. The row is the index — the searchable summary and the joins. The full material lives beside it: the verbatim transcript in Raw/, the processed note in Notes/. A meeting that is only in someone's memory is not in this registry, and that is the gap the module exists to close.

columns.name: title
columns.note: What the meeting was, in a line a search would find: 'Acme POC wrap-up', not 'sync'.

columns.name: related_type
columns.note: What this meeting was about. 'none' is a deliberate answer (an internal call, a conference conversation) — not a dodge for a meeting nobody matched. If the deal can't be identified, ask; don't file it as none to move on.

columns.name: related_id
columns.note: OPP-/REN-/CUST-/LEAD- id. Required the moment related_type names a record type — a meeting 'about an opportunity' with no opportunity named is unjoinable, and every downstream use (engagement, prep, commitments) needs the join.

columns.name: source
columns.note: Where the material came from. Zoom = pulled via the connector; Transcript File / Notes File = dropped into 13-Meetings/Inbox/; Pasted = given in conversation.

columns.name: raw_path
columns.note: The verbatim original in 13-Meetings/Raw/. Blank only for Pasted material the user chose not to keep — otherwise the raw is kept always, because the processed note is an interpretation and the original is the evidence behind it.

columns.name: notes_path
columns.note: The processed note in 13-Meetings/Notes/. A registry row with no note behind it is a claim with no substance.

columns.name: attendees_internal
columns.note: Semicolon-separated names, your side.

columns.name: attendees_external
columns.note: Semicolon-separated, customer side, as 'Name <email>' where the email is known — the email is what lets contact threading and engagement dedup work. Resolve it from opportunity-contacts where the transcript only gives a name.

columns.name: new_faces
columns.note: External attendees seen for the first time on this deal. A new face usually means the deal is widening or the champion is being second-guessed — either way worth a line in the note.

columns.name: summary
columns.note: Two or three sentences. What happened and what changed — written so that six months later, this row alone answers 'what was that meeting'.

columns.name: outcome
columns.note: A judgement, recorded as one. Advanced = something concrete moved (next step agreed, new stakeholder engaged, blocker cleared). A pleasant meeting where nothing moved is Neutral, however good it felt.

columns.name: sentiment
columns.note: How the customer sounded — a different question from `outcome`, which records whether the deal moved. The divergences are the signal: Positive sentiment with a Neutral outcome is the classic pleasant-meetings-no-deal pattern, and Negative with Advanced is a hard conversation that did its job. `Unclear` is a legitimate answer for a garbled transcript or a guarded room; reaching for it beats inventing a reading.

columns.name: sentiment_evidence
columns.note: What was actually said that supports the reading — a quote or close paraphrase, with the speaker. Required for any non-neutral sentiment: a sentiment with no evidence behind it is a vibe wearing a column name, and vibes are exactly what this registry exists to replace. Neutral and Unclear need no defence.

columns.name: tasks_raised
columns.note: Semicolon-separated TASK- ids raised from this meeting's action items.

columns.name: commitments_logged
columns.note: Rows written to the commitments registry from this meeting.

columns.name: key_quote
columns.note: The single most consequential thing said, verbatim, with the speaker. The full set lives in the note; this one is here so a registry search surfaces it.

columns.name: competitors_mentioned
columns.note: Semicolon-separated competitor names heard in the meeting. Each should also have been routed to competitor tracking — this column is the index, not the destination.

columns.name: risks
columns.note: Semicolon-separated, short. Deal-relevant challenges heard: a feature gap named as blocking, a budget wobble, a competitor gaining ground.

columns.name: positives
columns.note: Semicolon-separated, short. Buying signals heard: an advantage acknowledged, expansion interest, champion language.

columns.name: next_step
columns.note: The next step as agreed IN the meeting, in the customer's framing. What flows to the opportunity's next_step field once the user confirms it.

columns.name: next_meeting_date
columns.note: When a follow-up was agreed. Feeds prep: the daily brief reads this registry for the account before that day's meeting.

columns.name: engagement_ingested
columns.note: Whether this meeting reached the activity cache. 'already-on-calendar' means the calendar/CRM copy is already counted and ingesting again would risk double-counting the single highest-weighted event kind there is. 'ingested' means this was an off-calendar meeting and the transcript is the only record — the case where this module moves the engagement score at all.

columns.name: crm_activity_id
columns.note: Set when the meeting summary was logged to the CRM as an activity — with confirmation, like every push.
